commitMessage: governance: correct the Repair A authority envelope to the canonical prohibited-operation set

cohortSelfExclusion.reason: The consumption record cannot hash its own final bytes; its identity is bound by the authority and manifest instead.

cohort.reason: A.1. The single dependent binding. This record pins the final bytes of every path in the Repair A cohort, including the authority document itself, so correcting the authority necessarily moves one cohort entry sha256 and byteLength. Nothing else in the record is touched: the other twenty-five entries, the manifest digest, the base head and the consumed use all stay exactly as Repair A recorded them.
A.1. Exact two-path functional cohort with per-path pre-states taken from the live bytes immediately before the correction. No wildcard, no directory blanket, no unrelated path.

A.1. The Repair A authority declared fourteen prohibitedOperations: the twelve canonical values plus LEDGER_APPEND and GATE21_START. The canonical set is CLOSED-WORLD — the evaluator compares it by exact set equality — so two additions intended as extra restraint made the whole authority refusable, and VERIFY_PROGRAM_CONSUMPTION returned BLOCKED with PROHIBITED_OPERATIONS_INVALID. The two values are removed and nothing else in the document changes. The restraint they were meant to express is not lost: LEDGER_APPEND and GATE21_START were never permitted by this authority in the first place, because a maintenance program may only touch the exact paths its manifest names, and no ledger or GATE21 path appears there.

A.1. Single-use LOCAL_EXPLICIT_AUTHORITY for this correction. Editing an already-consumed authority document without an authority of its own would be precisely the self-authorization this framework exists to prevent.
